analysis: The method internal_write takes a byte[] src, int off, int len. Inside a while loop, System.arraycopy is called with src, off as srcPos, out_buffer as dest, out_buffer_pos as destPos, and copy as length. No null checks are performed on src or out_buffer before the call. The parameters off and len are not validated for non-negative values (though the loop condition len > 0 ensures len is positive before each call, but initial len could be negative and the loop would not execute). The computation of copy = min(len, space) ensures destPos+copy <= BUFF_SIZE (assuming out_buffer length is BUFF_SIZE), so dest bounds are safe. However, src bounds are not checked: off may be negative or off+copy may exceed src.length. ArrayStoreException is impossible because both src and dest are byte arrays.
answer: NullPointerException: not avoided (src or dest could be null). ArrayStoreException: avoided (byte[] to byte[]). IndexOutOfBoundsException: not avoided (off may be negative, off+copy may exceed src.length; also length negative is avoided by loop condition but off negative is not checked).
remark: NullPointerException can be thrown if the src parameter (passed as byte[] src) or the dest field (out_buffer) is null at the time of the call. IndexOutOfBoundsException can be thrown in two scenarios: (1) if off (srcPos) is negative, or (2) if off + copy (srcPos+length) exceeds src.length. Note that dest bounds are implicitly safe because copy is at most BUFF_SIZE - out_buffer_pos and out_buffer is assumed to have length BUFF_SIZE. ArrayStoreException is not thrown because both arrays have the same primitive component type (byte).
